description: Stochastic Dreams canonical verse corpus — 16 primary Odu, structured for the verse expansion engine.

A: Before the hall was full, the charter stone was struck.
The Map Maker sealed it — and every avenue aligned at once.
B: But ink that dries before the hall is full
writes law for those who came,
not those who could not come in time.
C: The threshold shines.
Somewhere beyond it, a name is missing from the register.
Q: Who will the next hand write into the margin?

A: The old house was let to fall.
Someone stood in its dust, listening
for what would feed on what was lost.
B: What decays in public sight
feeds something underneath the hearing —
but the tenants of the ruin
were not asked what they still needed from its walls.
C: Green shoots in the rubble.
A woman walks past carrying what she saved.
Q: Who decides what grows in the place of what was let go?

A: Every ledger in Lens Tower opened at once.
The Map Maker stood in the light and said: let the record speak.
B: What is seen cannot return to shade,
but shade was where the handshake lived,
where trust was made in rooms without a transcript.
C: The tower publishes. The bridge falls quiet.
A child reads the record and asks why the numbers don't match the story.
Q: Can the next hand build a room that holds both truth and tenderness?

A: Gate Quarter shut its mouth against the wind
and called the silence safety.
B: What is locked to save the well
also locks the well from rain.
The garden thrives one season,
then the soil turns to salt.
C: Inside, the ward breathes its own air.
Beyond the wall, a market learns to live without it.
Q: Will the gate open from the inside, or must the rain find another way?

A: A song was sung at the sealed archive
until the stone remembered it was a door.
The Path Finder entered first.
B: What returns from burial
brings its old companions:
the song, the grievance, and the map
that shows the road they were forbidden to walk.
C: The archive is open. Old rites return to public hearing.
A grandmother corrects the official history and no one can prove her wrong.
Q: Can the next hand hold what was returned without fearing what it remembers?

A: Contracts scattered in the air above the Loom Exchange
and the heirs grabbed thread without knowing its provenance.
B: Every scramble feels like freedom
to those who hated the old arrangement,
and like theft to those whose labour was woven into it.
C: The exchange hums with new deals, none of them signed.
Someone is weaving beautifully.
Someone else is searching for a pattern that no longer exists.
Q: Will the new cloth hold, or will it unravel at the first pull?

A: Every bowl at Feast Market was filled to the brim.
The Path Finder poured the last measure herself,
knowing the morning would ask where it went.
B: Generosity that cannot count
gives and gives until
the cupboard holds only the echo of a feast.
The morning after abundance is always a quiet room.
C: The table groans with shared bread.
In the granary, a child counts the remaining sacks on one hand.
Q: Who will plant before the warmth of the feast has cooled?

A: Signal Spire lit up before anyone could read the terms.
The Map Maker drew the frame at lightning speed
and the field complied.
B: Brilliance casts its shadow forward.
What leaps without looking
lands precisely on the ground
that someone else was standing on.
C: The spire blazes.
A district outside its permissions watches through the fence.
Q: Will the next hand widen the frame, or will the bright walls grow doors?

A: A blade was lifted in the Foundries.
The Map Maker held it steady
and asked no one which vein it was.
B: Every necessary cut
also severs something it did not intend.
The surgeon heals by choosing what to sacrifice,
and the sacrifice has a name.
C: The obstruction is cleared. The Foundries breathe again.
In the ward, a severed connection bleeds quietly into the floor.
Q: Was the cut clean enough to heal, or did it sever something load-bearing?

verses.title: The Mirror That Judges the Frame
verses.predicament: The Mirror That Judges the Frame

A: The Map Maker built the throne. The Path Finder brought the mirror.
What the ruler saw in it
was not the ruler's story.
B: A mirror cannot be uninvented.
Once the frame has seen its shadow,
it can pretend, but the pretending
now costs more than the truth.
C: Mirror Court falls silent.
Authority stands with its contradiction on public view,
and the crowd has not yet decided what to do.
Q: Will the next hand reform the frame, or shatter the glass?

A: The oath was read aloud in Bond Archive
and every signatory heard a different promise.
B: An oath kept past its season
binds the letter but releases the spirit.
Those who hold to the words most faithfully
betray the reason the words were spoken.
C: The compact is enforced.
Two districts honor the same clause and arrive at opposite actions.
Q: Can the next hand write new words, or are the old ones too sacred to touch?

A: The well was treated. The well was declared clean.
Underneath, the old seepage shifted its path.
B: A remedy that reaches only the surface
teaches the sickness to travel deeper.
The well ran clear for a season.
Then the taste changed again.
C: Reservoir Commons drinks and trusts the test.
In the lower aquifer, the contaminant adjusts.
Q: Will the next hand follow the water downward, or trust the surface reading?

A: The Map Maker said: frame it. The Path Finder said: let it stand raw.
The work was mounted in public light
and both stepped back to see what the room would do.
B: Not every truth survives its audience.
The artist who shows everything
wagers that the commons can hold
what the commons spent years hiding from itself.
C: Glass Agora is full. The work hangs in the open.
Half the room weeps. The other half looks for the exit.
Q: Will the next hand build a vessel for the truth, or will the truth dissolve?

A: The Path Finder held the seed another year.
The season did not come.
The vault stayed full and the ground stayed bare.
B: Patience, when it grows too long,
becomes the shape of refusal.
The seed preserved in perfect darkness
forgets what soil feels like.
C: Seed Vault is full and silent.
Outside, the ground is ready but unplanted.
A farmer asks: how many perfect seasons must pass before we risk the first?
Q: Will the next hand break the ground, or polish the seed for another year?

verses.title: The Festival on the Fault Line
verses.predicament: The Festival on the Fault Line

A: A drum was struck at Rhythm Court
and the commons rose to dance
on ground that had not finished grieving.
B: Joy laid over fracture
mends the ear but not the floor.
The music always stops eventually,
and what is underneath
does not care who was dancing.
C: Rhythm Court is luminous tonight.
Beneath the dance floor, a crack the builders know about widens by a finger.
Q: Will the next hand give the ground a voice, or will the music play louder?

A: The Map Maker and the Path Finder returned together to Origin Gate.
Each insisted the story had always been theirs.
The gate did not settle the argument.
B: The origin is never still.
Those who go back to recover what was
find instead what they now need it to have been.
No one returns to the same beginning twice.
C: Origin Gate stands open.
The myth the founders told is not the myth their children recognize.
Both versions are true. Neither is sufficient.
Q: Will the next hand write a new beginning, or learn to live with two?
